title: Policy Orchestrator: safe apply & rollback with role-scoped approvals and tamper-evident ledger
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Build a policy orchestration service that safely applies batching/caching recommendations and supports deterministic rollback with end-to-end auditability. This ticket covers: (1) role-scoped approval flows (fine-grained RBAC mapped to org IAM groups), (2) dry-run / sandbox execution with cost delta previews, (3) append-only tamper-evident ledger for all config changes, and (4) deterministic rollback artifacts and reverse deltas for fast failover. The goal is to enable the Optimize engine to auto-propose improvements while giving security/compliance teams cryptographically-verifiable trails and operators safe, auditable apply/rollback primitives.
acceptance_criteria: RBAC: changes require approver roles per policy; service enforces at least one approver for P2, two approvers for P1, and three approvers for P0 (sensitivity-driven).
Dry-run: every recommended change can be executed as a no-op in a sandbox that produces token-level cost delta estimates and latency impact projections visible in Console.
Ledger: all apply/rollback events are persisted to an append-only ledger (signed HMAC entries), stored encrypted in S3 with KMS, and an immutable index is queryable from Console.
Rollback: rollback produces deterministic reverse-delta artifacts, validated in a test sandbox before execution, and can be invoked via API or Console within the retention window.

Audit: every change includes correlation_id, actor, approvers, rationale, diff blob (before/after), and a link to the originating recommendation. Logs are retained per compliance settings and exportable for e-discovery.
Integration: integrates with existing Console rollout UI and sends PagerDuty alerts for failed auto-applies and rollbacks.
risks: If rollback reverse-deltas are non-idempotent, customer traffic could see inconsistent behavior—need strong validation and canary gating.
Ledger storage growth could increase S3 costs—plan retention tiers and tiered cold storage for old events.
Mis-specified RBAC rules could allow unauthorized applies—must include tests and an audit verification job.
updates: 2026-02-18: Initial ticket created after architecture review with product and security. Decision to use append-only ledger rather than DB soft-delete due to compliance needs.
2026-02-25: Design review — security requested HMAC + KMS-backed keys for ledger entries; product requested cost delta previews to be surfaced in Console before approval.
2026-03-03: Engineering spike completed validating deterministic reverse-delta generation for batchcache toggles. Found edge-case with partial KV cache hits; mitigation plan added to spec.
2026-03-08: Prototype PR opened for RBAC layer and dry-run simulator (see PR #4821). E2E tests for approval workflows added to CI pipeline but flaky under simulator load.
2026-03-10: Switched ledger storage plan to S3 + Glue index for searchability; retention policy draft set to 7 years for enterprise customers with option to configure shorter retention.
review_feedback: Security (Diego Alvarez): please include HSM-backed key rotation and split-knowledge for production ledger signing keys.
Product (Maya Lin): show expected monthly cost savings and worst-case rollback delta for each recommendation in the Console card.
Design (Rory Chen): UX should expose approver identity but redact email in exported reports for privacy; include reason code taxonomy.
implementation_notes: Plan to implement a small orchestration service (policy-orch) that receives recommendations from Optimize, creates a change-order object, simulates apply in a sandbox cluster, writes signed ledger record, then enqueues a staged apply to Dedicated clusters. Uses AWS KMS for encryption and HMAC via a rotating key. Canary strategy: 1% traffic for 30 minutes then 10% for 2 hours before full rollout; automated rollback if error rate > 0.5% or token latency regressions exceed configured SLO.
operational_runbook: How to investigate a failed auto-apply: correlate change-id in ledger, fetch dry-run results, check canary metrics in Console, escalate to SRE if rollback fails.
Performing manual rollback: use Console -> Change Orders -> select change -> Run rollback (requires approver role).
Key compromise mitigation: revoke current HMAC key, mark ledger range as 're-keyed', re-sign future entries and store re-key metadata.
